environment.description: Same Laravel 10 application deployed on GKE with Pod Security Standard 'restricted' profile enforced at namespace level via PodSecurity admission controller. Container image uses distroless PHP base. The pod spec sets securityContext.readOnlyRootFilesystem=true with NO tmpfs volumes, NO emptyDir volumes, and NO PVC mounts. The only writable path available to the process is /dev/null. Database connection uses the same RDS PostgreSQL instance but through a PgBouncer sidecar proxy configured with a prepared-statement query whitelist (pgbouncer.ini transaction_mode with server_prepared_statements=yes and a custom auth_query that maps to a PostgreSQL role restricted via row-level security policies and column-level UPDATE privileges that only permit modifications to: name, email, avatar_url, bio, notification_preferences columns on the users table).

config.container_security: readOnlyRootFilesystem=true, no tmpfs/emptyDir/PVC mounts, runAsNonRoot=true, allowPrivilegeEscalation=false
config.database_role: app_writer_restricted - PostgreSQL role with column-level GRANT UPDATE(name, email, avatar_url, bio, notification_preferences) ON users; no UPDATE privilege on is_admin, password, role, email_verified_at columns
config.row_level_security: enabled on users table, policy: USING (id = current_setting('app.current_user_id')::int)
config.network_policy: egress restricted to PgBouncer sidecar only (no direct DB access)
config.filesystem_note: Laravel session/cache configured for database driver since no writable filesystem available; log channel set to stderr
